title: C102C — Generator Connector Reference
introduction:
This sheet connects the generator connector’s identity, drawing and circuit assignment. The generator is the engine-driven electrical machine commonly called the alternator; it supplies vehicle power and charges the battery while running.

I start with the connector identifier, then follow the drawing’s cavity label into the assignment table. That label is the little signpost doing the useful work: it connects the pictured contact to the circuit, recorded wire details, function and terminal part number. The Fpn entry matches the Terminal Part Number entry, providing a cross-reference between the tables.

Use this page for identification and circuit-map reading. Physical viewing direction, access steps and electrical test conditions are outside its scope. The Gauge convention and meanings of Size and Used are unspecified, so preserve those entries as printed without using them alone to select wire or replacement parts.

edits.why: The illustration shows a labelled circular contact with an adjoining open, curved feature. Use the contact label to find the matching Cavity entry. Neither the connector name nor this drawing establishes a physical viewing direction.

The cavity row links the illustrated contact to its circuit, recorded wire fields, Function wording and terminal identifier. Read those fields together while retaining the original codes; they do not prescribe an electrical test or establish replacement compatibility.
